item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 290206
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores,
and on Tropical Storm Hanna, located well to the east-northeast of
Bermuda.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT3.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

...FAY REACHES TROPICAL STORM STRENGTH AGAIN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM AST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...26.0N 45.9W
ABOUT 1380 MI...2215 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 230 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1008 MB...29.77 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM AST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was 
located near latitude 26.0 North, longitude 45.9 West. Fay is moving 
toward the southwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A southwest to 
west-southwest motion, along with an increase in forward speed, is 
expected to continue over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Little change in strength is forecast during the next 
day or so, and Fay is forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone in 
36 h.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1008 mb (29.77 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 36
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 290236
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  36
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
1100 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026
 
The convection around Fay continues to improve during the evening
hours, but is still a bit sheared to the south of the low-level
center. A few cloud tops near -70 C persist, with the objective
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS in the range of 34-43 kt.
However, the latest TAFB Dvorak fix was a T2.0/30 kt. Based on the
given data, the intensity has been risen to 35 kt for this
advisory, which makes Fay a tropical storm again.
 
The storm is still moving toward the southwest with an estimated 
initial motion of 225/8 kt. This general southwest to west-southwest 
motion is expected to persist for the next couple of days as Fay is 
guided by the flow along the southern periphery of a mid-level 
ridge situated over the central Atlantic. The current NHC track 
forecast is very similar to the previous one with just a few minor 
adjustments based on the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.

The intensity of the cyclone is likely to continue to fluctuate 
for the next couple of days as convection continues to pulsate, but 
that convection will likely be sheared away from the center since 
SHIPS guidance indicates increasing shear over the next day or so. 
The global models still show that Fay will struggle to maintain 
deep convection once it moves into a more stable air mass and an 
area of upper-level convergence. The current NHC intensity forecast 
only shows minor changes in intensity with Fay becoming a
post-tropical cyclone in a day or so, then degenerate into a trough 
in a few days.

item.title: Tropical Storm Hanna Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT43 KNHC 290243
TCDAT3
 
Tropical Storm Hanna Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL082026
1100 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026
 
Satellite imagery shows Hanna's convective structure remains 
highly sheared with an exposed center. The deepest convection 
remains displaced to the east of the tropical storm's center due to 
strong westerly vertical wind shear. Subjective Dvorak estimates 
from TAFB came in at T2.0/30 kt, slightly below objective estimates 
ranging between 35 and 50 kt. Based on a blend of these data, the 
initial intensity is held at 40 kt.
 
The initial motion continues east-southeastward at 105/12 kt. Hanna 
is embedded in the flow between a longwave trough to its northeast 
and a larger subtropical ridge to its south. This synoptic pattern 
should result in a continued east-southeastward motion over the next 
24–36 hours with a gradual slowdown in the track as the mid-latitude 
trough leaves Hanna behind. Much of the track guidance then shows a 
slow east-northeastward motion after the cyclone becomes vertically 
shallow and influenced by a low-level ridge centered south of the 
Azores. The updated NHC track forecast is a blend of the previous 
advisory and the corrected consensus (HCCA) aid, nudging the track 
slightly southward.

Hanna is expected to remain in a hostile environment, with moderate 
to strong vertical wind shear prevailing over the next 48–72 h. 
However, because the tropical storm is generally moving in the same 
direction as the shear vector, deeper convection well east of the 
center may allow for slight intensification, as portrayed in some 
reliable guidance. SHIPS guidance indicates that vertical wind shear 
will only increase throughout the forecast period, while mid-level 
RH values show the storm being starved of moisture, which may weaken 
the system. Hanna is expected to be devoid of deep convection around 
the 60 h mark, degenerating into a post-tropical cyclone at that 
time.
